problem_statement: The bitfield module should provide three new functions: bf_find_first_set, bf_find_first_unset, and bf_set_all. bf_find_first_set must return the lowest index of a set bit in a bitfield when given a bitfield and a number of bits, or -1 if no bit in that range is set. bf_find_first_unset must return the lowest index of an unset bit in a bitfield when given a bitfield and a number of bits, or -1 if all bits in that range are set. bf_set_all must set every bit with an index less than the given number of bits to 1, using the existing bitfield bit numbering, and must not change bytes completely outside that bit range.

verification.reason: The statement gives the new functions and most of their behavior, but it does not clearly state that bits at indices greater than or equal to the given size must not be set, which the bf_set_all test checks through exact byte values.

problems.detail: The tests also verify that bits outside the requested bit range in the last partially covered byte are not set (e.g. high bits of field[0] for size 5 and high bits of field[3] for size 30), but the statement only says bytes completely outside the range must not be changed.

problem_statement_fixed: The bitfield module should provide three new functions: bf_find_first_set, bf_find_first_unset, and bf_set_all. bf_find_first_set must return the lowest index of a set bit in a bitfield when given a bitfield and a number of bits, or -1 if no bit in that range is set. bf_find_first_unset must return the lowest index of an unset bit in a bitfield when given a bitfield and a number of bits, or -1 if all bits in that range are set. bf_set_all must set every bit with an index less than the given number of bits to 1, using the existing bitfield bit numbering, and must not change bytes completely outside that bit range. It must not set any bit with an index greater than or equal to the given number of bits, including the upper bits of the last byte that intersects the range.
